findings.description: The journey model makes consumer optional, but the objective requires declaring the intended consumer family for consumer-facing outcomes. If omission remains valid, typing and consumer-surface validation can be bypassed before close-time enforcement ever sees stable vocabulary.

The seeded evidence rule depends on fixture_only, but the plan only says fixture_only is optional and does not pin its default. Missing fixture_only semantics can make seeded_masks_readiness nondeterministic for older or partially-authored journeys.

The typing function is specified for one surface_class, but journeys can declare multiple surfaces and consumer=both. The plan does not pin journey-level aggregation semantics that require at least one human-surface requirement and at least one agent-surface requirement to be satisfied together.

The structured_error rule depends on a degraded or error-path claim, but claim_kind is otherwise closed to read_only, mutation, and qualitative. There is no pinned input field that tells the pure typing rule when an error path is being evaluated.

The mutation requirement notation is ambiguous: the prose says idempotency plus rollback are both required, but the requirement-expression example could be read as alternatives or as malformed grouping.

F004 says degraded_dishonest only when neither family provides availability=unavailable for a required data_source, but the user journey requires both human and agent families to degrade honestly. One family could silently omit its degraded signal while the other family masks the failure.

The checker needs to compare human and agent EvidenceRefs by data_source, but EvidenceRef does not gain an explicit surface_class, consumer_family, or source-family attribution field. Inferring family from evidence_class is underspecified and breaks for shared classes such as structured_error.

F004 adds allowed_degraded_modes to the contract but never specifies how the checker validates or consumes those modes. That leaves an accepted schema field with no behavioral effect in the honesty gate.

The CLI transcript adapter is required to be non-interactive and no live paid call may be made, but the plan does not pin the command contract, fixture mode, or environment guard that prevents accidental paid external execution.

The contract names the typed-skip reason-location fix as D028, while F003 labels the same acceptance point as D029. This drift can cause implementers to miss the exact round-3 typing fix the objective says is in scope.

F002 references a close gate named F005 even though close-time enforcement is explicitly out of scope and delegated to sibling plan 2b. This creates an implementation target that is not part of the objective contract.

F002 says satisfaction matches evidence_class plus data_provenance, while F004 says availability=unavailable typed-skips must never satisfy a consumer-surface capture. Without an explicit shared rule, a degraded typed-skip carrying the required evidence_class could be counted as satisfied by the typing checker.

F004 requires degraded EvidenceRefs to use an allowed degraded mode, but neither F001 nor F004 defines a structured field on EvidenceRef that carries the selected degraded mode. That leaves the checker unable to enforce allowed_degraded_modes without reading prose.

F001 makes consumer_family optional even though F004 depends on per-family degradation and cross-family agreement. If availability-bearing EvidenceRefs omit consumer_family, the checker cannot reliably prove that each required family degraded honestly.

The typing matrix is only partially pinned. F002 gives example requirements for several surfaces, but it does not explicitly define read_only requirements for every closed surface_class, including interactive_ui, mobile_app, external_integration, and service_batch.

The MCP adapter acceptance pins tools/list but leaves the second read-only tool as an example such as list_projects or status. That makes the dogfood fixture dependent on whatever tool happens to exist, weakening deterministic harness tests.

The plan adds new agent EvidenceSource adapters, but F004 also requires human-family unavailable labels with structured data_source, availability, provenance, and consumer_family. The non-goal excludes rebuilding human-surface capture, yet no minimal compatibility path is specified.

F001 requires a total SurfaceFamily mapping, but the proposed plan does not pin the exact family for every closed surface_class member. Ambiguous cells like external_integration, service_batch, and backend-derived surfaces can change consumer x surface validation outcomes.

The journey.surfaces token mapping named in F001 lists web, backend, mcp_tool, cli_agent, and cli_human, but does not pin tokens for mobile_app or external_integration even though those are closed surface_class values and mobile human capture already exists.

F002 states that agent_mcp_tool read_only success is satisfied by tool_call_transcript or contract_check, but the listed tests do not include the required unit-test-only mismatch and transcript-satisfied agent API/MCP cases from the journey contract.

F003 typed-skip EvidenceRefs specify availability=unavailable and data_provenance=degraded, but do not require data_source, consumer_family, or degraded_mode, which F001/F004 need for validation and per-family degradation checks.

The no-secret assertion is pinned only for the MCP transcript path, while the required evidence asks harness tests for all three agent adapters to be no-secret. CLI and contract artifacts could leak secret-shaped fields without violating the written F003 acceptance.

F004 describes a pure checker mostly at the journey evidence-set level, but the contract requires human and agent journeys for the same objective to agree by shared data_source key. The objective-level collection and comparison boundary is not pinned.

EvidenceRef data_provenance is optional for compatibility, but F002 does not define how consumer-readiness evidence with an evidence_class and missing data_provenance is handled. That leaves seeded-versus-real enforcement dependent on implementation choices.

F001 says each journey.surfaces token maps to a pinned surface_class, but the token web maps to read_only_ui|interactive_ui. That is not a total deterministic mapping and makes downstream evidence derivation ambiguous.

F002 defines journey-level requirements as the UNION of per-surface groups, which can collapse identical groups across different declared surfaces. A single contract_check or screenshot could then appear to cover multiple surfaces without proving each surface.

F003 requires successful adapter outputs to set type, evidence_class, and data_provenance, but only typed-skips are explicitly required to carry data_source, availability, and consumer_family. That leaves successful agent evidence structurally weaker than the shared EvidenceRef vocabulary defined in F001.

The objective contract requires missing-provenance closes to be flagged, but F002's checker statuses only name satisfied, evidence_class_mismatch, and seeded_masks_readiness. Missing data_provenance is fail-closed, but the observable result is not pinned.

The required evidence calls for consumer and fixture_only validation tests, but F001 only explicitly lists consumer validation tests. fixture_only has a default and is used by F002, yet malformed fixture_only input is not called out for validation.

F002 requires each declared surface to be satisfied independently and each EvidenceRef to be consumed by at most one surface group, but neither F001 nor F002 defines a structural surface or surface-instance binding on EvidenceRef or the checker input. With two surfaces sharing screenshot or contract_check requirements, aggregation would rely on caller convention or data_source inference.

F002 describes the checker input as evidence_class plus data_provenance, but also requires availability=unavailable typed-skips to never satisfy a capture. The checker cannot enforce that shared exclusion unless it receives availability, or the full EvidenceRef, so a degraded typed-skip path remains under-specified.

Claim-kind ownership is split across the plan: the objective journey names read_only, mutation, and qualitative, while F002 extends claim_kind with error_path and F001 does not define or validate one closed ClaimKind enum. Implementations could reject error_path at journey validation or accept unpinned values.

F001 says every legacy qa-sufficiency class maps 1:1 to a surface_class, but also says the legacy mutation class is not a surface_class and is modeled as claim_kind=mutation. That leaves legacy mutation-labelled journeys with ambiguous migration behavior against the total-map invariant.

F003 pins the MCP read-only tool to status, but the CLI transcript adapter and schema/contract check remain generic. Without exact argv, offline environment contract, contract target files, and output schemas, implementations can produce divergent artifacts while still claiming compliance.

F003 does not explicitly require successful or typed-skip adapter EvidenceRefs to carry EvidenceRef.surface_class, while F002 makes missing surface_class structurally ineligible for satisfying any surface group.

F002 requires availability, consumer_family, surface_class, and data_provenance for evidence to satisfy readiness, but the plan does not define how existing human-surface screenshot or recording producers will populate those new fields.

The typed-skip shape is described, but validation is not fully pinned against malformed unavailable evidence such as unavailable plus real provenance, missing degraded_mode, missing reason note, or missing evidence_class.

The pinned token map still has an ambiguity: it claims a total deterministic map over eight journey surface tokens but writes ios/android as a combined token, which leaves the accepted token domain unclear.

The checker returns a single status even though journey-level aggregation can create multiple independent per-surface and conjunctive-group failures, so mixed missing_provenance, seeded, and mismatch cases are not deterministic.

F002's scoped legacy_untyped rule lets human-family EvidenceRefs missing the new typed fields return not_yet_typed, but the objective still requires UI substrate-only and seeded-only cases to produce evidence_class_mismatch or seeded_masks_readiness in this plan.

F001 requires a schema VERSION bump for the new EvidenceRef vocabulary, while F003 pins the contract-check adapter to agent-conventions v1.0 schema models. That can make the dogfood contract check validate stale schemas and miss the new fields.

F001 says the journey surface-token map covers only eight surface tokens, but the pinned accepted token list contains nine tokens and also discusses legacy-8 migration after excluding mutation and splitting CLI.
F001 states degraded_mode is required when an EvidenceRef represents a degraded data_source, but the dedicated malformed validation cases only enumerate typed-skip availability=unavailable failures.

The plan defines required_evidence_classes(surface_class, consumer, claim_kind), but the F002 requirement matrix is keyed primarily by surface_class and does not explicitly specify behavior for invalid single-surface tuples such as consumer=agent with read_only_ui, or consumer=human with agent_mcp_tool. F001 validates journeys, but the pure typing API can still be implemented in a way that ignores consumer.

EvidenceRef carries both surface_class and consumer_family, while F001 also pins a deterministic surface_class-to-family mapping. The proposed validators require consumer_family when availability is set, but they do not explicitly reject EvidenceRefs whose consumer_family conflicts with the pinned family for their surface_class. That leaves room for structurally contradictory evidence to enter F002/F004.

The journey aggregation is keyed by surface_class, but F001 intentionally maps multiple journey surface tokens to the same surface_class, most notably ios and android to mobile_app. If a journey declares both tokens, EvidenceRef.surface_class alone cannot prove which platform was exercised, even though each declared surface is supposed to be satisfied independently.

The ClaimKind domain is inconsistent between the objective journey, which names read_only, mutation, and qualitative, and F001/F002, which add error_path to the closed enum. Because the enum is closed, this is not harmless wording; implementation could either reject a contract-valid value set or accept an out-of-contract value.

The plan validates consumer=both at the journey level, but F002 does not pin how required_evidence_classes handles consumer=both for a single surface_class. The invalid-tuple rules only discuss consumer=human and consumer=agent, leaving ambiguity between passing both through, decomposing by surface family, or rejecting it.

F001 requires every evidence_class to map to a valid existing EvidenceRef.type, but the proposed features do not pin the full mapping table. F003 gives examples for agent transcripts and contract checks, but human, mutation, and structured evidence classes remain implementation-defined.

The qualitative claim rule is not fully specified across the surface and consumer matrix. F002 says qualitative returns rubric or human_signoff, but does not state whether that replaces or adds to the surface base, and it creates an unclear requirement for agent-family qualitative claims.

The plan allows journey.consumer=both, but F002's required_evidence_classes API is defined over a single consumer value and only pins invalid-tuple behavior for human and agent. It does not state whether consumer=both is accepted per surface, rewritten into the surface's pinned family, or rejected at the pure-function boundary.

The qualitative claim_kind cell is not coherent across the closed surface_class enum. F002 states qualitative returns rubric|human_signoff, but agent-family surfaces with consumer=agent are otherwise valid tuples and would be asked to satisfy a human-only evidence group.

F002 contains conflicting aggregation language: it says aggregation granularity is surface_class and same-class tokens form one group, but also says each declared surface forms its own requirement set and groups are not deduplicated across surfaces. This leaves ios+android and other same-class token cases ambiguous.

F001 requires a documented evidence_class to existing EvidenceRef.type table, but the proposed feature does not pin the table cells for the full closed evidence_class enum. F003 only constrains the agent subset, leaving human, mutation, and structured classes open to inconsistent implementation choices.

F001 says consumer is required for journeys asserting a consumer-facing outcome, but the plan does not define the structural signal used to determine that a journey is consumer-facing. Without that discriminator, omission rejection can drift between always-required and heuristically-required behavior.

reason: After eight paid sufficiency rounds, all structural findings have been resolved. Remaining findings are exhaustive invariant/matrix enumeration over already-defined closed enums and rules: ClaimKind objective-contract alignment, consumer=both single-surface behavior, evidence_class->EvidenceRef.type mapping table, and qualitative surface x consumer matrix. These are accepted as implementation obligations, not design blockers. Locking via operator override; implementation must pin each with exhaustive equality/matrix tests before close.
